plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE (confounded batch, labeled)
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 lung RNA-seq samples (6 treated in batch B2, 6 control in batch B1), raw salmon-derived gene counts. The batch is perfectly confounded with condition, so any batch-adjustment or correction method (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA) would remove the condition effect along with the batch and cannot be used; the model matrix with both terms is not full rank. Per the confounding rule, the plan proceeds with a condition-only model (~condition) under the explicit, stated assumption that batch does not systematically differ from the biological condition, and every downstream result is labeled 'confounded by batch — cannot separate biological treatment effect from processing batch effect.' Track 1 runs standard sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap colored by both condition and batch, to visualize that the two are inseparable), then DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization, minimal count pre-filter, DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log2FC shrinkage, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05, with count-outlier flagging reported. Track 2 takes the ranked full gene list (Wald statistic) and runs fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) with Reactome as a stated follow-up collection, both under the same confounding caveat. A final report step consolidates DE results, fit diagnostics, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a reproducibility record, and repeats the confounding caveat prominently as the analysis's central limitation.
